A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Fly-CL work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-H are readable, allowing retained material to be matched across additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original continual-learning evaluations, including accuracy, training time, memory consumption, ablations, and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds baseline evaluations, forgetting measurements, projection diagnostics, and experiments with additional backbone configurations.

M1.justification: Sparse projection, top-k filtering, streaming statistics, GCV regularization selection, and Cholesky-based ridge classification remain unchanged, as do Algorithms 1-2. Section 6 introduces an equivalent Hebbian learning formulation but explicitly retains direct ridge solving rather than implementing those learning dynamics.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate image classification on CIFAR-100, CUB-200-2011, VTAB, ImageNet-R, and ImageNet-A, including the retained online and domain-shift settings. New backbone configurations and feature diagnostics use existing coverage. Proposed LLM and reinforcement-learning applications remain future work.

E2.justification: v2 adds InfLoRA, SEMA, and MoE-Adapter to the evaluated comparators in Tables 1, 5, 6, and 8, substantially expanding comparisons to LoRA/adapter methods. Existing comparators remain. The new SDM discussion does not constitute an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: v2 introduces backward-transfer evaluation, experiments using Qwen2.5-VL-7B's vision encoder, and a normalized pairwise-distance diagnostic using 500 sampled CIFAR-100 feature vectors. Additional sensitivity sweeps extend the evaluation design. Existing dataset splits, task schedules, and default hyperparameters remain unchanged; final-stage accuracy was already used in v1.

E4.justification: Appendix B.1 adds an empirical distance-preservation test absent from v1. Appendices C.7-C.8 extend the original CUB/ViT sensitivity analysis to ImageNet-A, longer CUB task sequences, ResNet-50, and projection-dimension sensitivity with Qwen features. These substantially broaden checks of geometric preservation and hyperparameter robustness.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five random seeds and mean plus or minus standard deviation in Appendix E.3. Added results retain this reporting convention; no changed run counts, confidence-interval procedures, or significance tests are stated.

E6.justification: Matched numerical entries in Tables 1-9 are retained, but v2 adds comparator scores, geometric and sensitivity findings, and Tables 10-11. Table 10 reports Fly-CL backward transfer of -3.82, -3.80, and -2.01 on CIFAR-100, CUB, and VTAB. Table 11 adds Qwen-backed accuracies of 95.06%, 94.68%, and 97.45%; these use a different backbone and are not same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: New Section 6 derives the ridge stationary solution from supervised Hebbian/anti-Hebbian updates with weight decay, introducing Equations 13-17. Section 4.2 also corrects the thin-SVD orthogonality identities to U^T U = V^T V = I_r. The original sparsity theorems and Appendix B proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and efficiency-versus-accuracy claims remain substantively stable. The introduction strengthens the biological subclaim: v1 asks whether the KC-to-MBON pathway supports decorrelation, while v2 claims a theoretical connection through consistency between Hebbian learning and ridge classification.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds a substantive mechanism explanation connecting Hebbian strengthening, anti-Hebbian error correction, and homeostatic decay to the ridge classifier. New appendix discussions interpret geometric preservation and backbone scalability. Appendix F expands prospective applicability to LLM-informed representations, reinforcement learning, and adaptive sampling without reporting experiments in those domains.

D1.justification: Appendix E.1 explicitly documents ImageNet-21K pretraining followed by ImageNet-1K fine-tuning for ViT; the checkpoint link itself is unchanged. Appendix B.1 specifies sampling and projection normalization for the new diagnostic. Existing code/data links, implementation settings, and hardware disclosures remain, while details for the added baselines and Qwen experiments are limited.

R1.justification: v2 expands positioning through LoRA/adapter literature and method descriptions, a dedicated comparison with Kanerva's sparse distributed memory, and cited connections to LLM/RL applications. Hebbian-learning and Qwen references are added, while Ryali et al. (2020) is removed. The FlyLoRA publication update represents the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: The introduction and method explanations receive localized edits. v2 inserts a discussion section, additional appendix subsections, acknowledgments, ethics and reproducibility statements, and a conference header. Most existing prose and the overall section sequence remain intact; the revision is primarily additive rather than an extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds a distance-distortion histogram, four sensitivity figures, and tables for final accuracy/backward transfer and backbone comparisons. Tables 1, 5, 6, and 8 gain comparator rows. Existing figures are retained, with original Figures 6-8 becoming Figures 7-9; the new displays substantially expand the visual evidence.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation by adding adapter competitors, directly measuring forgetting, and testing projection geometry and sensitivity beyond v1's original CUB/ViT analysis. Section 6 also makes the biological rationale explicit through a ridge stationary-point derivation. These address important evidence and explanation gaps while retaining the original results. New comparator/backbone implementation details remain limited, and the Qwen experiments establish accuracy rather than an additional latency advantage.
